editorial_holds: Research title is 1662–1797, not previously misstated 1662–1779. Gimpel 1982 note 11 can contain the 1779 variant but official Historical Commission contents take precedence.
Ketteler 1931 p270 has been cited by Saxon Academy but was not opened as a scanned page in this research. No firsthand original guild name list seen.
1719 Anton Reinhard Neuhaus was admitted, not rejected; religion/denomination UNKNOWN. Amtsohn is reported admission category, not evidence of a confessional exclusion.
Gimpel 1982 says citizen oath precondition and discrepancies up to two years between guild and treasury entries, but exact 1670 and 1777 archival leaves not read.
Original municipal 1662–1797 guild record shelfmark remains unknown; printed edition is a different source object.
Historic building the Dutch housed in 1648 is a contextual location, not proof any treaty clause was litigated by a later guild applicant.
1810 corporation abolition, 1823 meeting and 1824 property disposal are distinct events, as is 1797 published series endpoint.
142 members in an 1823 summary referring to 1810 is not annual admissions count; no full cohort or statistical series computed.
No public image, full modern book pages, original guild folios or photo rights published. Keep main/AI Studio unchanged.
